page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.large is a high clock speed virtual server instance powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor running at a base clock frequency of 3.1 GHz. The instance operates under the KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical CPU core with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). It is configured with 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation (2.0 GB per core). The hardware includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache, with instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512 (including AVX512F and AVX512_VNNI), and AES-NI.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures and standard compute execution. Network connectivity provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned by default.

Benchmark measurements reflect the entry-level core allocation. While single-threaded tests such as Geekbench single-core (1263.0) and stress-ng single-core (1429.79) position in the average range, multi-core metrics sit in the lowest percentiles due to the two-vCPU hardware footprint. PassMark CPU score reaches 2342.0, Geekbench multi-core scores 1507.0, and stress-ng multi-core achieves 1903.59. Memory tests show 13.21 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 12.1 GB/sec write bandwidth. Workload throughput tests demonstrate 1.88 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.15 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

Given the dual-thread single-core physical design and 4 GB RAM footprint, Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.large is positioned for compute tasks requiring elevated per-core clock frequency and AVX-512 extensions without requiring heavy memory or massive parallelism. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web microservices, single-threaded processing pipelines, and small utility or batch processing jobs.
